newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican official says peso volatility "normal".
newsitem.headline: Mexican official says peso volatility "normal".

text.p: The Mexican peso's recent volatility is normal and should die down as soon as the currency reaches a level the market finds comfortable, a top Finance Ministry offical said on Wednesday.
"Volaltility like we are seeing is normal in these types of markets," Alejandro Valenzuela, chief spokesman for the government's economic recovery program, told a news conference.

"This volatility was predictable, because investors felt that sooner or later the peso had to depreciate due mostly to the differences between inflation rates in Mexico and other countries, mainly the United States," he said.
Mexico's peso has fallen from about 7.52 per dollar to just under 7.80 per dollar in the past week in part due to worries that it was getting too strong.

Valenzuela said volatility is normal after long periods of exchange rate stability. But he stressed that the free-floating system is working properly and that the central bank was not interfering to support the peso.

"It is important to keep in mind the system is working properly ... today, for example, when the peso fell to its session low, investors began selling dollars to take advantage of the cheap peso," he said.
"As the market finds a new level for the peso, volatility will die down. Maybe we are already at that level, maybe the peso needs to adjust more, we don't know," he added.
